web_evidence.title: Authorial economics in fiction: A study of authors in Colleen Hoover's Verity (2018)
web_evidence.note: Scholarly textual analysis explicitly identifies Lowen’s first-person narration and Verity’s first-person narration in the embedded fictionalized autobiography.

web_evidence.title: Verity Summary and Study Guide
web_evidence.note: The overview explicitly says the novel transitions between Verity’s and Lowen’s first-person points of view.

web_evidence.title: Colleen Hoover Writing Styles in Verity
web_evidence.note: The point-of-view analysis states that the novel has two narrators, with Lowen narrating in first person and Verity’s narration contained in her memoir and letter.

web_evidence.title: Verity Reading Group Guide
web_evidence.note: The publisher’s guide corroborates the structural distinction between Lowen’s experience and Verity’s embedded autobiography, but it does not independently state the grammatical person.

web_evidence.title: Verity
web_evidence.note: The author’s official synopsis verifies the work, Lowen’s role, and the embedded unfinished autobiography, but does not explicitly describe narrative person.

person_note: The controlling narrative is Lowen’s participating first-person account, repeatedly exposed by event narration and exterior dialogue beats using “I” and “me.” The novel also contains substantial passages from Verity’s memoir and letter, but research establishes that these embedded texts are likewise first person. Multiple narrators in the same grammatical person remain FIRST rather than ALTERNATING under the methodology. Dialogue, aphorisms, and generic “you” statements were not treated as narrator evidence. The quote snippets do not always reveal whether a first-person passage belongs to Lowen or Verity, but the whole-book structural sources resolve that uncertainty, and no credible third- or second-person narrative strand was found.
